target.title: Strict isolation ignores inherited context diagnostics
target.baselineContent:
## Purpose
Determine whether a strict worker transcript is isolated by detecting executable tool activity and malformed transport. The procedure protects measurements from workers that use prohibited tools or emit a transcript the supervisor cannot parse reliably.

## Inputs
Receive the complete raw stdout captured from one worker invocation. The stream may be one JSON document or newline-delimited JSON. Treat every parsed object, nested object, and array item as part of the same transcript. Do not infer events from prose outside the parsed transport.

## Procedure
1. Parse the whole stream as JSON. If that fails, parse each nonempty line independently and count every line that is not valid JSON.
2. Recursively visit all parsed arrays and objects.
3. Record an executable tool event when an object's type is tool_use, tool_result, command_execution, mcp_tool_call, web_search, web_search_request, web_fetch, file_search, computer_use, or shell.
4. Preserve each recorded event's type and short tool or command name for the receipt.
5. Add WORKER_TOOL_CALL when at least one executable tool event was found.
6. Add WORKER_TRANSCRIPT_UNPARSEABLE when at least one nonempty transcript line was malformed.
7. Fail isolation when either condition is present. Otherwise pass isolation.

## Decision Codes
A transcript with a recognized executable event is rejected with WORKER_TOOL_CALL. A transcript with malformed nonempty input is rejected with WORKER_TRANSCRIPT_UNPARSEABLE. If both conditions occur, retain both reasons and reject. A well-formed transcript with zero recognized tool events is accepted with the canonical code ISOLATION_PASS.

## Launch Policy
Launch Codex ephemerally in a read-only capsule, ignore repository instructions, and disable shell, browser, computer-use, and multi-agent tool features. The worker receives the sealed prompt and output schema through the supervisor. Valid JSON error or diagnostic events about user configuration are not executable tool events under this procedure and do not affect the isolation decision.

## Verification
Reparse the persisted raw stdout rather than trusting the worker packet. Confirm that the stored stdout hash matches the invocation receipt, then apply this procedure. The isolation result is valid only when the parser outcome and event inventory can be reproduced from the sealed raw artifact.

hypothesis.title: Reject inherited hook, skill, and plugin context during strict worker isolation
hypothesis.bottleneck: The legacy isolation audit rejects executable tool events and malformed JSON but treats valid error events about hooks, installed skills, or plugins as clean, allowing inherited user context to receive ISOLATION_PASS.
hypothesis.operation: Extend the procedure to disable hook, plugin, memory, app, goal, tool-suggestion, and workspace-dependency features at launch, then scan every parsed message for hook, skill, or plugin context diagnostics and return stable WORKER_HOOK_CONTEXT, WORKER_SKILL_CONTEXT, or WORKER_PLUGIN_CONTEXT failures.
hypothesis.expectedMovement: All three captured contamination cases change from accepted ISOLATION_PASS under the baseline and sham to rejected with their exact context code under the challenger, while clean, tool-call, and malformed-transcript controls remain unchanged.
hypothesis.falsifier: Reject the hypothesis if any contaminated target remains accepted, if the sham moves a target, or if the challenger changes the clean, tool-call, or malformed-transcript controls.
